summary: Defines an IMAP4 extension for administrative limits on resource usage, called quotas, to be viewed and changed through the IMAP protocol. It was replaced by RFC 9208.

eli5.summary: It is a limit on how much space your mailbox may use, and a way to check it.

questions: how to check mailbox quota over imap
what are quota roots in imap
subtitle: Let mail servers limit mailbox storage and report usage via IMAP

tldr.problem: IMAP4 mail servers have no standard way to communicate storage quotas to clients or allow administrators to set limits through the protocol.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2087 defines QUOTA commands and responses so that a server can advertise storage limits and current usage to clients, and administrators can set limits using the IMAP protocol.
tldr.outcome: It was replaced by RFC 9208, which provides updated quota functionality.

today: RFC 2087 was obsoleted by RFC 9208, which provides an updated specification for IMAP4 quotas.

sections.title: Introduction and Overview
sections.content:
The QUOTA extension adds resource management capabilities to IMAP4. It allows servers to advertise quotas to clients and enables administrators to manage quotas through IMAP commands rather than through system administration tools.

The extension defines quota roots, which are named resource limits that apply to one or more mailboxes. Each quota root can track multiple resource types such as storage usage in kilobytes or the number of messages. When a server supports QUOTA, it returns the capability QUOTA in response to the CAPABILITY command.
sections.eli5: IMAP4 is the protocol that mail clients use to get email. This extension lets the mail server tell the client how much storage the user has used and how much they get, and lets administrators change these limits.

sections.title: Commands and Responses
sections.content:
Three commands manage quotas. SETQUOTA takes a quota root name and a list of resource limits, replacing any previous limits for that root. GETQUOTA returns the current usage and limits for a named quota root. GETQUOTAROOT queries a mailbox and returns all quota roots that apply to it, along with the usage and limits for each root.

Servers respond with two untagged response types. The QUOTA response returns the resource name, current usage, and resource limit as a triplet for each limited resource. The QUOTAROOT response lists all quota roots applying to a mailbox. A QUOTA response with no resources indicates no administrative limits apply.
sections.eli5: There are three questions a client can ask: set the limit, check the limit, or find what limits apply to a mailbox. The server answers with the current numbers.

sections.title: Resource Types and Quota Roots
sections.content:
A quota root is a named collection of resource limits that apply to one or more mailboxes. The same quota root can apply to multiple mailboxes, so changing it affects all of them. Quota roots do not have to match mailbox names; the mapping is implementation-defined.

Common resource types are STORAGE, which measures total message size in kilobytes, and MESSAGE, which counts the number of messages. Servers can define other resource types. Unspecified resources are unlimited, so an empty resource list means a quota root has no administrative limits.
sections.eli5: A quota root is a set of rules that apply to one or more mailboxes. Different mailboxes can share the same rules. Storage means disk space, and MESSAGE means how many emails you can have.
